chunks: He said: The Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) said: The Messenger of Allah (blessings of Allah upon him and his family) sent an expedition. When they returned, he said: Greetings to a people who have completed the lesser struggle, yet the greater struggle remains upon them. It was said: O Messenger of Allah, what is the greater struggle? He said: The struggle against the self. Then he said: The best struggle is when one struggles against the self that is between his two sides.

key_terms.الْجِهَادَ الْأَصْغَرَ: the lesser struggle -- referring to external military expeditions
key_terms.الْجِهَادُ الْأَكْبَرُ: the greater struggle -- the inner spiritual struggle against one's base desires
key_terms.جِهَادُ النَّفْسِ: struggle against the self -- the perpetual effort to discipline the ego (nafs)
key_terms.سَرِيَّةً: expedition -- a military detachment sent by the Prophet

ai.seo_question: What did Prophet Muhammad say about the greater jihad versus the lesser jihad?
ai.summary: The Commander of the Faithful narrates that the Prophet welcomed his companions back from a military expedition, telling them they had completed the lesser jihad but the greater jihad remained. When asked what the greater jihad was, he replied it was the struggle against one's own self (nafs), adding that the noblest form of struggle is that of a person against the self dwelling between his two sides. This teaching reframes the concept of jihad from external warfare to the inner spiritual discipline of self-purification -- a central theme in Islamic ethics that would have deeply resonated with the companions who had just experienced battle.

en.bilal-muhammad: He said: Amir al-Mu’minin (as) said: The Messenger of Allah (s) sent people on an expedition. When they returned, he said: Greetings to a people who completed the minor struggle (jihad); the major struggle remains for them. It was said: O Messenger of Allah! What is the major struggle? He said: The struggle against the self. Then, he (s) said: The best struggle is the struggle against the self that is between his two sides.
